name: related_result: ctdnalit-20261011-helzer2025-protocol-grail-full
description: Descriptive fact transcribed from the pinned source.

attributes.value: In silico mixing of GRAIL-cohort cancer and healthy reads (70% training, 30% validation; mixtures 50:50 to 1:99 at 100 M reads) showed all metrics losing AUROC as ctDNA fraction fell, with depth at all exons best; at 0.0001-0.001 ctDNA fraction many AUROCs approached 0.5. The values are shown only in Figure 6B and are not stored as results.
attributes.source_locator: Results P15-P17; Figure 6; Methods P31

review.reviewer_note: Separate Claude review agent (reviewer-ctdna), independent of the extractor uc-ctdna; no human review claimed
review.method_note: Hand transcription from the article text, checked by string match in extract/extract_helzer2025.py.
review.note: Re-downloaded the pinned artifacts and matched their SHA-256; compared all 790 cells with a separate parser of the pdftotext layout text written for this review (the extractor's script was not run), with panel blocks fixed by row order, every Mean AUROC checked against its row mean and the UW column order checked from the word bounding boxes of the rotated header; compared 44 values by eye against rendered pages 8 and 9 of the PDF.

name: Helzer et al. 2025 Razavi et al. 2019 GRAIL cohort, FoundationOne Liquid CDx gene subset: multinomial phenotype AUROC
description: Panel fragmentomic metrics computed on only genes shared with the FoundationOne Liquid CDx panel; one multinomial model per metric predicts Breast, Lung, Normal, Prostate.

attributes.protocol: For each metric, a GLMnet multinomial model is trained and scored by 10-fold cross-validation with the same folds for every metric, repeated with 25 seeds; the reported AUROC per phenotype is the median over the 25 replicates, and 'Mean AUROC' is the mean over phenotypes. Features use only genes shared with the FoundationOne Liquid CDx panel.
attributes.version: Helzer et al. 2025, Supplementary Table S1 (PDF caption), block 'FoundationOne Liquid CDx'
limitations: Targeted exon-panel sequencing of metastatic cancers, not whole-genome sequencing of a screening population.
AUROC values are medians over 25 replicates of 10-fold cross-validation; no interval is printed.

Methods P23 names GLMnet multinomial logistic regression for cancer-type and cancer-vs-healthy predictions; whether the 'Normal' (healthy vs all cancers) AUROC comes from the multinomial model or a separate binary model is not stated.
The authors state that the study compares metrics rather than producing a locked prediction model.

The article text cites the UW cohort results as Table S1 and the GRAIL results as Table S2, but the supplementary PDF captions label the GRAIL table S1 and the UW table S2. Locators here follow the PDF captions; the values quoted in the text match the tables as captioned in the PDF.
The Figure 4 and 5 legends call the plotted value the average AUROC of 25 repeats; the table captions and Methods P23 say median. Values here follow the tables.

name: Relevance of ctdnalit-20261011-helzer2025-protocol-grail-full to "Which fragmentomics workflow detects tumour-derived plasma DNA under realistic low tumour fractions and fixed false-positive constraints?"
description: Compares many fragmentomic metric classes, adapted to exon panels by the authors, (length, depth, end motifs, TFBS and open-chromatin entropy, Griffin in the UW cohort) on the same plasma samples with one classifier and shared folds. Proxy: inputs are targeted exon panels rather than whole-genome sequencing, the cancers are metastatic, the endpoint is AUROC without a fixed false-positive constraint, and the low-tumour-fraction analysis is figure-only.

attributes.endpoint: Healthy vs all-cancer one-vs-rest AUROC (and per-cancer-type AUROC) for 12 fragmentomic metrics and their combination on the same targeted-panel cfDNA samples, same folds: Razavi et al. 2019 GRAIL cohort, full panel
attributes.rationale: Compares many fragmentomic metric classes, adapted to exon panels by the authors, (length, depth, end motifs, TFBS and open-chromatin entropy, Griffin in the UW cohort) on the same plasma samples with one classifier and shared folds. Proxy: inputs are targeted exon panels rather than whole-genome sequencing, the cancers are metastatic, the endpoint is AUROC without a fixed false-positive constraint, and the low-tumour-fraction analysis is figure-only.
constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and preserved limitations before citing a result.
Use the 'Normal' (healthy vs all cancers) results for detection; the other columns are cancer-type or subtype discrimination.
Do not combine with whole-genome fragmentomics results from other protocols; panel, cohort and classifier differ.
limitations: Targeted exon-panel sequencing of metastatic cancers, not whole-genome sequencing of a screening population.
AUROC values are medians over 25 replicates of 10-fold cross-validation; no interval is printed.

Methods P23 names GLMnet multinomial logistic regression for cancer-type and cancer-vs-healthy predictions; whether the 'Normal' (healthy vs all cancers) AUROC comes from the multinomial model or a separate binary model is not stated.
The authors state that the study compares metrics rather than producing a locked prediction model.

The article text cites the UW cohort results as Table S1 and the GRAIL results as Table S2, but the supplementary PDF captions label the GRAIL table S1 and the UW table S2. Locators here follow the PDF captions; the values quoted in the text match the tables as captioned in the PDF.
The Figure 4 and 5 legends call the plotted value the average AUROC of 25 repeats; the table captions and Methods P23 say median. Values here follow the tables.
